column3: Close to the Greek; “letter of divorce” is rendered “certificate of divorce.”
Close to the Greek; NKJV adds “for any reason” before “except,” and “causes her to be adulterated” becomes “causes her to commit adultery.”
Close to the Greek; “the evil” is rendered “the evil one,” though the Greek may also mean “evil.”
Close to the Greek; “strike” is rendered “slaps.”

NKJV follows the Textus Receptus, which adds “bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you” and “spitefully use you”; the critical text has only “love your enemies and pray for those persecuting you.”
NKJV reads “tax collectors” in the second question, following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “Gentiles.” NKJV adds “than others.”
NKJV reads “your Father in heaven,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “your heavenly Father.”
